title: God Takes Care of Me
verse: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
reflection: A good shepherd leads his sheep to food and water and keeps them safe. The LORD cares for His people the same way, so with Him we have everything we truly need.

title: Be Strong and Brave
verse: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
reflection: God said this to Joshua just before he led Israel into a new land. Courage is not the same as never feeling afraid; it is remembering that God goes with you wherever you go.

title: Be Still and Trust God
verse: Be still, and know that I am God.
reflection: When life gets noisy and worrying, God invites us to stop, quiet our hearts and remember who He is. He is in control, even when we are not.

title: God Is Love
verse: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
reflection: Love is not only something God does; it is who He is. When we love others, we show that we know Him.

title: Don't Be Afraid, God Is With You
verse: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God.
reflection: God does not promise that storms will never come, but He promises to be with us in them. Because He is our God, we do not need to be dismayed.

title: This Is the Day God Made
verse: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
reflection: Every day is a gift from God, not just the easy ones. We can choose to rejoice in today because the LORD made it.

title: God's Word Lights My Way
verse: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
reflection: A small lamp lights up just enough of the path to take the next step. God's word shows us how to live, one step at a time.

title: I Can Do All Things Through Christ
verse: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
reflection: Paul wrote this after learning to be content whether he had plenty or very little. Our strength for whatever comes is not our own; it comes from Christ.

title: Always Be Joyful in the Lord
verse: Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.
reflection: Paul wrote these joyful words while he was in chains. Joy in the Lord does not depend on how things are going around us.

title: Keep On Praying
verse: Pray without ceasing.
reflection: Praying without ceasing means staying close to God all through the day, talking to Him about everything, big or small, wherever you are.

title: Love One Another
verse: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
reflection: Jesus gave His disciples this new commandment on the night before He died. He did not only tell us to love one another; He showed us how.

title: Be Kind to One Another
verse: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another.
reflection: Kindness, a tender heart and forgiveness belong together. The verse goes on, "even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you": we forgive because we have been forgiven.

title: With God All Things Are Possible
verse: With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
reflection: Jesus said this when His disciples wondered who could ever be saved. What is impossible for people is never too hard for God.

title: God's Joy Makes Me Strong
verse: for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
reflection: Nehemiah said this to people who were weeping as they heard God's law read. Real strength comes from the gladness of knowing God, not from how strong we feel.

title: Trust God with All Your Heart
verse: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
reflection: Our own understanding only sees part of the picture. Trusting God with all our heart means relying on Him even when we do not understand, and the next verse promises that "he shall direct thy paths."

title: Let Your Light Shine
verse: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
reflection: Jesus said His followers are like a light that cannot be hidden. When people see our good works, the aim is not that they praise us but that they "glorify your Father which is in heaven."

title: Taste and See That God Is Good
verse: O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
reflection: You cannot know how good food is until you taste it. In the same way, David invites us to trust God for ourselves and find out how good He is.

title: Walk by Faith, Not by Sight
verse: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)
reflection: Faith means trusting God even when we cannot see what lies ahead. We follow His promises, not only what our eyes can tell us.

title: God's Mercy Is New Every Morning
verse: his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
reflection: These words were written in a very sad time, after Jerusalem had been destroyed. Even then the writer remembered that God's mercies never run out: every morning brings new ones.

title: God Will Never Leave You
verse: I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
reflection: God promises never to leave or forsake His people. Because of that promise, the next verse says, we may boldly say, "The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear."

title: Give All Your Worries to God
verse: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
reflection: Worries can feel like a heavy bundle we carry everywhere. God invites us to hand every care over to Him, because He really does care for us.

title: Give Thanks, God Is Good
verse: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
reflection: Giving thanks reminds us where every good thing comes from. God is good, and His mercy never runs out, so there is always something to thank Him for.

title: A Happy Heart Is Good Medicine
verse: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.
reflection: A cheerful heart helps us and the people around us, almost like medicine. Joy and laughter are good gifts from God.

title: God Is My Light
verse: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
reflection: When things seem dark or scary, God is like a light that chases the shadows away. With the LORD on our side, we do not need to be afraid.

title: God Made Me Wonderfully
verse: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works
reflection: God made you with great care, every part of you, down to the tiniest detail. You can praise Him for the way He made you.

title: Put God First
verse: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
reflection: Jesus said not to worry about food or clothes, because God feeds the birds and dresses the lilies. When we put God first, He takes care of what we need.

title: God Is My Safe Place
verse: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
reflection: A refuge is a safe place to run to. When trouble comes, God is not far away; He is "a very present help," right there with us.

title: Be a Peacemaker
verse: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
reflection: Peacemakers help people stop quarrelling and become friends again. Jesus said they will be called the children of God.

title: A Gentle Answer Calms Anger
verse: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
reflection: Angry words make a fight bigger, but a gentle answer can calm things down. Next time someone is upset with you, try answering softly.

title: Love Your Neighbour
verse: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
reflection: Jesus said this is the second great commandment, after loving God. Loving our neighbour means treating others the way we would want to be treated.

title: Noah Built the Ark
verse: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
reflection: In a world full of violence, Noah walked with God. He built the ark just as God commanded, and he and his family were kept safe through the flood.

title: Abraham Trusted God's Promise
verse: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them.
reflection: God promised Abraham, who had no children, that his family would be as many as the stars. Abraham believed the LORD, and God "counted it to him for righteousness."

title: Joseph Forgave His Brothers
verse: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.
reflection: Joseph was sold as a slave by his brothers and later thrown into prison, yet he rose to rule in Egypt and saved many lives in a famine. He forgave his brothers, seeing that God had turned their evil into good.

title: Moses Led the Way Through the Sea
verse: Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.
reflection: Trapped between the Red Sea and Pharaoh's army, the people were terrified. Moses told them to stand still and watch, and God opened a dry path through the sea.

title: Miriam Sang for Joy
verse: And Miriam the prophetess … took a timbrel in her hand … And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously.
reflection: After God brought Israel safely through the sea, Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron, took a timbrel and led the women in singing and dancing to praise the LORD.

title: Joshua Chose to Serve God
verse: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.
reflection: After leading Israel into the promised land, Joshua asked the people to choose whom they would serve. He made his own choice clear: he and his family would serve the LORD.

title: Caleb Trusted God Fully
verse: Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
reflection: Ten of the spies said the people of Canaan were too strong, but Caleb trusted God's promise. Because he "wholly followed the LORD," he lived to receive his own inheritance in the land.

title: Deborah Led with Courage
verse: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah … And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day.
reflection: Deborah was a prophetess who judged Israel as she sat under a palm tree. She called Barak to lead the army and went with him, trusting God's word that the victory was His.

title: Gideon Won with 300
verse: and they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.
reflection: Gideon felt small and afraid, yet God called him a "mighty man of valour." With only three hundred men, trumpets, pitchers and lamps, Gideon saw God win the battle.

title: Ruth Stayed Loyal
verse: for whither thou goest, I will go.
reflection: Ruth, a young widow from Moab, refused to leave her mother-in-law Naomi and chose Naomi's God as her own. God blessed her loyalty, and she became the great-grandmother of King David.

title: Hannah Prayed with All Her Heart
verse: For this child I prayed. … his mother made him a little coat.
reflection: Hannah poured out her heart to God for a son, and God answered her prayer. She gave Samuel to serve the LORD, and every year she made him a little coat and brought it to him.

title: Samuel Listened to God
verse: Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
reflection: As a boy serving under Eli the priest, Samuel heard God call his name in the night. His answer is a good prayer for anyone: Speak, LORD, I am listening.

title: David Faced the Giant
verse: and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook … for the battle is the LORD's.
reflection: The shepherd boy David faced the giant Goliath with only a sling and five smooth stones. He knew the battle belonged to the LORD, not to swords and spears.

title: Elijah Stood Up for God
verse: Then the fire of the LORD fell … they said, The LORD, he is the God.
reflection: On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal. When fire fell from heaven and burned up the sacrifice, the people fell on their faces and cried, "The LORD, he is the God."

title: Esther Was Brave for Her People
verse: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
reflection: Esther became queen of Persia at just the right moment. When her people were in danger, she bravely went to the king to plead for them, even though it could have cost her life.

title: Nehemiah Rebuilt the Wall
verse: And they said, Let us rise up and build.
reflection: Nehemiah heard that the walls of Jerusalem lay in ruins. He prayed, asked the king for help and led the people to rebuild, and the wall was finished in fifty-two days.

title: Daniel Kept On Praying
verse: no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.
reflection: Daniel kept praying to God three times a day, even when it was against the law. He was thrown into the lions' den, and he came out without a scratch because he trusted God.

title: Three Friends Would Not Bow Down
verse: our God whom we serve is able to deliver us. … walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt.
reflection: The three friends would not bow down to the king's golden image. Thrown into a burning fiery furnace, they were seen walking in the fire unharmed, and a fourth man was with them.

title: Jonah Got a Second Chance
verse: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. … Salvation is of the LORD.
reflection: Jonah ran away from God's call, but God sent a great fish to swallow him. Inside the fish Jonah prayed, and God gave him a second chance to carry His message to Nineveh.

title: Zacchaeus Climbed Up to See Jesus
verse: and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him … Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down.
reflection: Zacchaeus was a rich chief tax collector, too short to see Jesus over the crowd, so he climbed a tree. Jesus called him by name and came to his house, and Zacchaeus gave half of his goods to the poor.

title: Peter Walked on Water
verse: he walked on the water … he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him.
reflection: Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water toward Jesus. When he looked at the wind he grew afraid and began to sink, but Jesus reached out at once and caught him.

title: Paul Never Gave Up
verse: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
reflection: Near the end of his life, Paul looked back on everything he had been through and said he had finished his course. He encourages us to keep the faith all the way to the end.

title: Sarah Laughed for Joy
verse: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.
reflection: Sarah waited many years for a child, and she even laughed when God said she would have a son in her old age. When Isaac was born, her laughter became pure joy.

title: Rebekah Watered the Camels
verse: I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.
reflection: When a traveller asked Rebekah for a drink, she gave him water and then kept drawing water for all his thirsty camels too. Her kindness went far beyond what was asked.

title: Jacob Dreamed of a Ladder to Heaven
verse: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest
reflection: Running away from home, Jacob slept on the ground with a stone for a pillow. God met him in a dream and promised, "I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest."

title: Elisha Carried On God's Work
verse: I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.
reflection: Elisha stayed close to Elijah to the very end and asked for a double portion of his spirit. After Elijah was taken up, Elisha picked up his mantle and carried on God's work.

title: The Servant Girl Who Spoke Up
verse: a little maid; and she waited on Naaman's wife. And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.
reflection: A young girl taken far from home could have been bitter, but she cared about the master of the house who was sick. Her few brave words led Naaman to God's prophet and to healing.

title: Josiah Became King at Eight
verse: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign … And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
reflection: Josiah became king when he was only eight years old. He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, which shows that you are never too young to follow God.

title: Dorcas Sewed Coats for Others
verse: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
reflection: Dorcas was always doing good, sewing coats and garments for widows who needed them. Her kindness was so loved that people showed Peter the clothes she had made.

title: Lydia Listened with an Open Heart
verse: a seller of purple … whose heart the Lord opened
reflection: Lydia sold fine purple cloth, but the best thing that happened to her was by a riverside, where the Lord opened her heart to hear the good news.

title: Barnabas Cheered Others On
verse: Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,)
reflection: Barnabas means "The son of consolation," someone who comforts and encourages. He stood up for Paul when others were afraid of him, and he gave generously to people in need.

title: Timothy Learned God's Word as a Child
verse: And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures
reflection: Timothy learned the scriptures from a child, taught by his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. He grew up to work alongside Paul and to lead others in the faith.

title: Methuselah Lived 969 Years
verse: And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died.
reflection: Methuselah lived 969 years, the longest life recorded in the Bible. He was the grandfather of Noah.

title: The Shortest Verse
verse: Jesus wept.
reflection: John 11:35 is the shortest verse in the KJV. Jesus wept at the grave of His friend Lazarus, which shows how much He cares about our sorrow.

title: The Longest Chapter
reflection: Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible, with 176 verses. Nearly every verse speaks about God's word: His law, statutes, commandments and testimonies.

title: The Shortest Chapter
verse: O praise the LORD, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people. For his merciful kindness is great toward us: and the truth of the LORD endureth for ever. Praise ye the LORD.
reflection: Psalm 117 is the shortest chapter in the Bible, with only two verses. In just a few words it calls all nations to praise the LORD for His merciful kindness and truth.

title: 66 Books in One Bible
reflection: The Bible is a library of 66 books: 39 in the Old Testament and 27 in the New. They were written over many centuries, yet they tell one story of God and His people.

title: How Tall Was Goliath?
verse: Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
reflection: Six cubits and a span is about nine and a half feet (almost 3 metres), if a cubit is about 18 inches. Goliath was a giant, yet young David defeated him.

title: The Ark Was Huge!
verse: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
reflection: If a cubit is about 18 inches, the ark was roughly 450 feet long, 75 feet wide and 45 feet high, big enough for Noah's family and all the animals God sent.

title: A Donkey That Talked
verse: And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam.
reflection: When Balaam struck his donkey three times, the LORD let the donkey speak. She had seen the angel of the LORD standing in the way, which Balaam could not see.

title: Samson Beat a Lion
verse: a young lion roared against him … and he had nothing in his hand.
reflection: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Samson, and he tore a young lion apart with his bare hands. Later, bees made honey inside its carcass, and that became Samson's riddle.

title: Elijah Went Up in a Whirlwind
verse: there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire … and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
reflection: Elijah did not die. A chariot of fire and horses of fire parted him from Elisha, and Elijah was taken up to heaven by a whirlwind.

title: Enoch Walked with God
verse: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.
reflection: Enoch did not die either: he walked with God, and God took him. Hebrews 11:5 says that before he was taken, "he pleased God."

title: Lunch for Five Thousand
verse: We have here but five loaves, and two fishes … they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full. And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children.
reflection: Jesus fed about five thousand men, besides women and children, with five loaves and two fishes, and there were twelve baskets of leftovers.

title: The Day the Sun Stood Still
verse: And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed.
reflection: When Joshua prayed during a battle, the sun stood still and the moon stayed until Israel had won. The Bible says there was "no day like that before it or after it."

title: The Shadow Went Backward
verse: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down in the dial of Ahaz.
reflection: God gave King Hezekiah a sign that he would be healed: the shadow on the dial of Ahaz went back ten degrees. God added fifteen years to his life.

title: Birds Brought Dinner
verse: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
reflection: During a long drought, God sent ravens to bring Elijah bread and meat every morning and evening while he stayed by the brook Cherith.

title: A Book That Never Says “God”
reflection: The book of Esther never mentions God by name, yet His care for His people can be seen all through the story, as Esther is in the right place at just the right time.

title: Every Letter but J
verse: And I, even I Artaxerxes the king, do make a decree to all the treasurers which are beyond the river, that whatsoever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, shall require of you, it be done speedily,
reflection: Ezra 7:21 in the KJV uses every letter of the English alphabet except J. It is part of King Artaxerxes' decree giving Ezra whatever he needed for God's work.

title: 3,000 Proverbs and 1,005 Songs
verse: And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.
reflection: King Solomon spoke 3,000 proverbs and wrote 1,005 songs. God had given him wisdom, understanding and "largeness of heart."

title: Every Hair Is Counted
verse: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
reflection: God knows you so well that He has numbered every hair on your head. Jesus said this to show that we are worth more than many sparrows, so we need not fear.

title: Manna Tasted Like Honey Wafers
verse: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.
reflection: Manna was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey. God sent it six days a week for forty years while Israel was in the wilderness.

title: A Giant's Iron Bed
verse: his bedstead was a bedstead of iron … nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it
reflection: Og, king of Bashan, was the last of a race of giants. His iron bed was nine cubits long and four wide, about 13½ feet by 6 feet if a cubit is about 18 inches.

title: Six Fingers and Six Toes
verse: a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number
reflection: A giant from Gath had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all. He was defeated by Jonathan, the nephew of David.

title: The Floating Axe Head
verse: And he cut down a stick, and cast it in thither; and the iron did swim.
reflection: One of the sons of the prophets lost a borrowed axe head in the river Jordan. Elisha threw a stick into the water, and the heavy iron floated to the top.

title: Shoes That Lasted 40 Years
verse: your clothes are not waxen old upon you, and thy shoe is not waxen old upon thy foot.
reflection: For forty years in the wilderness, God kept Israel's clothes and shoes from wearing out. He took care of even the smallest needs.

title: 153 Fish in One Net
verse: full of great fishes … and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken.
reflection: After the risen Jesus told the disciples where to cast the net, they caught 153 great fishes, and even with so many, the net did not break.

title: Moses' Glowing Face
verse: Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him.
reflection: After Moses spent time with God on Mount Sinai, his face shone so brightly that he covered it with a veil, and he did not even know it was shining.

title: Lefty Slingers Never Missed
verse: there were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded; every one could sling stones at an hair breadth, and not miss.
reflection: In the tribe of Benjamin there were 700 chosen lefthanded men who could sling a stone at a hair and not miss. That is amazing aim!

title: Absalom's Heavy Hair
verse: he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king's weight.
reflection: Absalom, a son of King David, cut his hair once a year because it grew so heavy. It weighed 200 shekels, a few pounds of hair.

title: 276 Shipwrecked, All Saved
verse: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls. … And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
reflection: Paul was on a ship of 276 people that was wrecked in a storm. Just as God had promised, not one was lost: some swam and some floated on boards, and they all escaped safe to land.

title: The Earth Hangs on Nothing
verse: He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.
reflection: Long ago the book of Job said that God "hangeth the earth upon nothing." The earth really does float in space, held by the power of its Creator.

title: Genesis
verse: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
reflection: The book of beginnings: creation, the first people, the flood, and the stories of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.

title: Exodus
verse: and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land
reflection: God rescues Israel from slavery in Egypt, parts the Red Sea and gives the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai.

title: Leviticus
verse: ye shall be holy; for I am holy
reflection: God's instructions for offerings, priests and holy living, so that a holy God could dwell among His people.

title: Numbers
verse: Every man of the children of Israel shall pitch by his own standard
reflection: Israel is counted and camped by tribes, then wanders forty years in the wilderness because the people did not trust God.

title: Deuteronomy
verse: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD
reflection: Before Israel enters the promised land, Moses reminds the people of God's law and calls them to love the LORD with all their heart.

title: Joshua
verse: the wall fell down flat
reflection: Joshua leads Israel into the promised land, the walls of Jericho fall flat, and the land is shared out among the tribes.

title: Judges
verse: The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon
reflection: Again and again Israel turns away from God, and again and again He raises up judges such as Deborah, Gideon and Samson to rescue them.

title: Ruth
verse: Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn
reflection: A story of loyalty and kindness: Ruth gleans in the fields of Boaz, who marries her, and she becomes an ancestor of King David.

title: 1 Samuel
verse: and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook
reflection: Samuel, the last of the judges, anoints Saul as Israel's first king and later anoints young David, who defeats Goliath.

title: 2 Samuel
verse: the sweet psalmist of Israel
reflection: The reign of King David, "the sweet psalmist of Israel": his victories, his sin and repentance, and God's promise of a lasting kingdom.

title: 1 Kings
verse: So Solomon built the house, and finished it
reflection: Solomon's wisdom and the building of the house of the LORD, then the kingdom splits in two and Elijah stands against the worship of Baal.

title: 2 Kings
verse: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full
reflection: The miracles of Elisha, like the widow's oil that kept flowing until every vessel was full, and the fall of Israel and Judah to their enemies.

title: 1 Chronicles
verse: These are their generations
reflection: Long family records from Adam onward, then the story of David's reign and his preparations for the house of God.

title: 2 Chronicles
verse: the fire came down from heaven
reflection: The kings of Judah from Solomon to the exile. When Solomon finished praying at the dedication of the house of the LORD, fire came down from heaven.

title: Ezra
verse: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD
reflection: Exiles return from Babylon to rebuild the house of God, and Ezra the scribe teaches them God's law.

title: Nehemiah
verse: every one with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon
reflection: Nehemiah leads the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls, with the builders working with one hand and holding a weapon in the other.

title: Esther
verse: for such a time as this
reflection: Queen Esther bravely risks her life to save her people from Haman's wicked plot.

title: Job
verse: When the morning stars sang together
reflection: Job loses almost everything yet will not curse God. The LORD answers him out of the whirlwind and gives him twice as much as he had before.

title: Psalms
verse: Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD
reflection: One hundred and fifty songs and prayers of praise, thanks, sorrow and trust, many of them written by David.

title: Proverbs
verse: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise
reflection: Short, wise sayings for everyday life, many from King Solomon, teaching that "the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge."

title: Ecclesiastes
verse: To every thing there is a season
reflection: The Preacher searches for meaning in everything "under the sun" and concludes: "Fear God, and keep his commandments."

title: Song of Solomon
verse: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys
reflection: A song of love between a bridegroom and his bride, full of gardens, flowers and pictures of springtime.

title: Isaiah
verse: they shall mount up with wings as eagles
reflection: The prophet Isaiah sees the LORD's holiness, brings comfort to His people and tells of a coming King whose name shall be called Wonderful.

title: Jeremiah
verse: as the clay is in the potter's hand
reflection: Jeremiah warns Judah to turn back to God before Jerusalem falls, and learns that God shapes His people like a potter shapes clay.

title: Lamentations
verse: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness
reflection: Poems of sorrow over the fall of Jerusalem, with a bright ray of hope in the middle: God's mercies are new every morning.

title: Ezekiel
verse: as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel
reflection: A priest among the exiles sees amazing visions: wheels within wheels, and a valley of dry bones coming back to life.

title: Daniel
verse: My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths
reflection: Daniel and his friends stay faithful in Babylon. God shuts the lions' mouths and shows the future through dreams and visions.

title: Hosea
verse: I will be as the dew unto Israel: he shall grow as the lily
reflection: Hosea's own family becomes a picture of God's faithful love for unfaithful Israel, and God promises to heal them and make them grow like the lily.

title: Joel
verse: I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten
reflection: After a plague of locusts, Joel calls the people back to God, who promises to restore what was lost and to pour out His spirit.

title: Amos
verse: a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand
reflection: Amos, a herdman from Tekoa, warns Israel that God is measuring His people with a plumbline and calls them to do what is right.

title: Obadiah
verse: though thou set thy nest among the stars
reflection: The shortest book of the Old Testament warns proud Edom that no place is high enough to hide from God, not even a nest among the stars.

title: Jonah
verse: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish
reflection: Jonah runs from God, is swallowed by a great fish, and at last preaches to Nineveh, where the whole city turns from its evil way.

title: Micah
verse: they shall beat their swords into plowshares
reflection: Micah sees a day of peace when swords become plowshares, and sums up what God asks: "to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God."

title: Nahum
verse: Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings
reflection: Nahum announces the fall of cruel Nineveh and good tidings for God's people, for "The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble."

title: Habakkuk
verse: he will make my feet like hinds' feet
reflection: Habakkuk asks God hard questions, waits for the answer, and ends by rejoicing in the LORD even if the fields and flocks should fail.

title: Zephaniah
verse: he will joy over thee with singing
reflection: A warning about the day of the LORD that ends with a beautiful picture of God rejoicing over His people with singing.

title: Haggai
verse: Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house
reflection: Haggai urges the returned exiles to stop putting off God's work and finish rebuilding His house.

title: Zechariah
verse: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts
reflection: Visions that encourage the rebuilders: the work will be done "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit."

title: Malachi
verse: if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing
reflection: The last book of the Old Testament calls the people to give God their best and promises a blessing poured out from the windows of heaven.

title: Matthew
verse: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid
reflection: The life and teaching of Jesus, the promised King, including His great teaching on the mount: "Ye are the light of the world."

title: Mark
verse: Peace, be still
reflection: The shortest Gospel, fast-moving and full of action, showing Jesus' power over sickness, storms and even death.

title: Luke
verse: Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost
reflection: A careful, orderly account of Jesus' life, with parables such as the lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son.

title: John
verse: I am the vine, ye are the branches
reflection: Written "that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God," with sayings such as "I am the vine" and "I am the light of the world."

title: Acts
verse: and ye shall be witnesses unto me … unto the uttermost part of the earth
reflection: How the good news of Jesus spread from Jerusalem toward the uttermost part of the earth through Peter, Paul and many other witnesses.

title: Romans
verse: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God
reflection: Paul explains the good news: all have sinned, and we are made right with God through faith in Jesus Christ, who makes all things work together for good.

title: 1 Corinthians
verse: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity
reflection: Paul writes to the believers at Corinth about living together in love, including the great chapter on charity: faith, hope and charity, and the greatest is charity.

title: 2 Corinthians
verse: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels
reflection: Paul writes about weakness and strength: God keeps His treasure in plain "earthen vessels" so that the power is clearly His.

title: Galatians
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace
reflection: Paul teaches freedom in Christ and describes the fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace and more.

title: Ephesians
verse: Put on the whole armour of God
reflection: Paul describes the riches believers have in Christ and tells them to put on the whole armour of God.

title: Philippians
verse: I press toward the mark for the prize
reflection: A joyful letter written from prison: rejoice in the Lord, and keep pressing on toward the prize.

title: Colossians
verse: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith
reflection: Christ is above all things, so believers should stay rooted and built up in Him, like a tree with deep roots.

title: 1 Thessalonians
verse: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout … and with the trump of God
reflection: Paul encourages young believers and comforts them with the hope of the Lord's return.

title: 2 Thessalonians
verse: But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing
reflection: Paul tells believers to stand firm, work quietly and never grow weary in doing good.

title: 1 Timothy
verse: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers
reflection: Paul's letter to young Timothy: do not let anyone look down on your youth, but be an example in how you live.

title: 2 Timothy
verse: All scripture is given by inspiration of God
reflection: Written near the end of Paul's life, urging Timothy to hold on to the Scriptures, which are given by inspiration of God.

title: Titus
verse: In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works
reflection: Paul tells Titus, left on the island of Crete, to teach sound doctrine and to be a pattern of good works.

title: Philemon
verse: Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved
reflection: A short, personal letter asking Philemon to welcome back Onesimus, his servant, as a brother beloved.

title: Hebrews
verse: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast
reflection: Jesus is greater than the angels, Moses and the priests. Chapter 11 remembers the heroes of faith, and our hope is an anchor for the soul.

title: James
verse: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only
reflection: A practical letter: real faith shows in what we do, so be doers of the word and not hearers only.

title: 1 Peter
verse: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house
reflection: Peter encourages believers who are suffering: they are lively stones, built together into God's spiritual house.

title: 2 Peter
verse: until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts
reflection: Peter urges believers to grow in grace and hold on to God's sure word, "a light that shineth in a dark place."

title: 1 John
verse: God is light, and in him is no darkness at all
reflection: God is light and God is love. John wrote so that believers may know that they have eternal life.

title: 2 John
verse: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth
reflection: A short letter to "the elect lady and her children," rejoicing that they walk in truth and urging them to love one another.

title: 3 John
verse: I wish above all things that thou mayest prosper and be in health
reflection: John writes to his friend Gaius, wishing him good health and praising his kindness to travelling believers.

title: Jude
verse: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling
reflection: A short letter warning against false teachers that ends with praise to the God who is able to keep us from falling.

title: Revelation
verse: a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal … the tree of life
reflection: John's vision of things to come, ending with a new heaven and a new earth, the river of the water of life and the tree of life.

title: Love
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
reflection: Love comes first in the list. It means caring for others the way God cares for us, choosing what is good for them even when it costs us something.

title: Joy
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
reflection: Joy is a deep gladness that comes from knowing God. It can stay with us even on hard days, when everyday happiness runs out.

title: Peace
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
reflection: Peace is a calm heart that trusts God. It also means getting along with others and making things right after a quarrel.

title: Patience
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
reflection: Patience (the KJV says "longsuffering") means waiting calmly for a long time, with people, with problems and with plans, without giving up or losing your temper.

title: Kindness
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
reflection: Kindness (the KJV says "gentleness") means being warm and tender with others, using soft words and careful hands instead of harsh ones.

title: Goodness
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
reflection: Goodness is doing what is right and helping others, even when no one is watching.

title: Faithfulness
verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
reflection: Faithfulness (the KJV says "faith") means trusting God and being faithful in return: keeping your word and staying loyal to God and to others.

title: Gentleness
verse: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
reflection: Gentleness (the KJV says "meekness") is not weakness. It is strength under control: being humble, teachable and slow to fight back. Moses was called "very meek."

title: Self-Control
verse: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
reflection: Self-control (the KJV says "temperance") means saying no to too much of anything and keeping our feelings and wants in check.

title: Belt of Truth
verse: Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness;
reflection: A soldier's belt (the KJV says "loins girt about") held the rest of his armour in place. Truth holds our lives together: being honest, and holding fast to what God says is true.

title: Breastplate of Righteousness
verse: Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness;
reflection: A breastplate guards the heart. Living right before God guards our hearts against the attacks of wrong.

title: Shoes of Peace
verse: And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace;
reflection: Good shoes keep a soldier steady and ready to move. The good news of peace with God gives us firm footing and makes us ready to share it.

title: Shield of Faith
verse: Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
reflection: Faith in God is like a shield that stops the fiery darts of the wicked: doubts, fears and temptations.

title: Helmet of Salvation
verse: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:
reflection: A helmet protects the head. Knowing that God has saved us guards our thoughts and fills us with hope.

title: Sword of the Spirit
verse: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:
reflection: The sword of the Spirit is the word of God. When Jesus was tempted, He answered each time with "It is written."

title: I Need God's Word Every Day
verse: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
reflection: Bread keeps our bodies going, but Jesus said we need something more. God's words feed our souls, so we need them every day, just like breakfast.

title: Grow Strong on God's Word
verse: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:
reflection: A baby wants milk because milk helps it grow. Peter says we should want God's word the same way, because reading it helps us grow strong inside.

title: Sweeter Than Honey
verse: How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
reflection: Honey was the sweetest treat people had in Bible times. The psalm writer loved God's words even more than that, and the more we read them, the more we enjoy them.

title: God Gives Me a Sound Mind
verse: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
reflection: Fear can make our thoughts race and our knees shake. God doesn't give us a fearful spirit; He gives power, love and a clear, steady mind.

title: Keep Your Mind on God
verse: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
reflection: Isaiah says God keeps in perfect peace the person whose mind is fixed on Him. When worries crowd in, thinking about God and trusting Him brings calm.

title: My Body Belongs to God
verse: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?
reflection: Paul says a believer's body is a temple, a home for God's Holy Spirit. That makes our bodies precious, so we use our hands, feet, eyes and words in ways that honour Him.

title: Godliness Helps in Everything
verse: For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.
reflection: Exercise is good for our bodies for a while, but Paul says godliness, living God's way, helps us in everything, now and forever. So we train our hearts as well as our muscles.

title: God Always Makes a Way Out
verse: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
reflection: Everyone is tempted to do wrong sometimes. God is faithful: He won't let the test be too big for us, and He always shows a way out so we can choose what is right.

title: Watch and Pray
verse: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
reflection: Jesus told His friends to watch and pray, because wanting to do right isn't always enough. Praying ahead of time and staying alert helps us stand strong when temptation comes.

title: Peace Is Better Than a Feast
verse: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife.
reflection: A plain piece of bread eaten together in peace is better than a huge feast full of arguing. Kind words and calm hearts make any home a happy place.

title: Feed on What Is Good
verse: Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.
reflection: God asked why people spend their money and hard work on things that never satisfy. He invites us to listen to Him, because what He gives truly fills the soul.

title: Good Friends Sharpen Each Other
verse: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
reflection: When one iron blade rubs against another, both get sharper. Good friends do that too: they encourage us, help us learn and make us better.

title: Get Back Up Again
verse: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
reflection: Everyone falls, sometimes over and over. Proverbs says the person who follows God gets back up again, so a mistake doesn't have to be the end of the story.

title: Never Give Up Doing Good
verse: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
reflection: Doing good can feel tiring when nothing seems to change. Like a farmer waiting for harvest, if we keep going, good things will grow in God's time.

title: Make Up Your Mind to Do Right
verse: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
reflection: Daniel was far from home in a king's palace, and he decided in his heart, ahead of time, to stay true to God. Deciding what is right before the test comes makes it easier to stand firm.
